stem: A 40-year-old man has thick, silvery-scaled plaques on his elbows and knees, and scale removal leaves tiny bleeding points. His dermatologist prescribes calcipotriene cream to apply to the plaques.
oneliner: 40M + silvery plaques on elbows and knees + pinpoint bleeding on scale removal + topical calcipotriene → how does it work?
ask: Which action best explains the drug's benefit?

options.A: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, limiting folate-dependent DNA synthesis
options.B: Neutralizes interleukin-17A and interrupts the T-cell cytokine loop
options.C: Inhibits calcineurin in T cells to block interleukin-2 transcription
options.D: Binds retinoic acid receptors to thin the stratum corneum
options.E: Activates the vitamin D receptor in keratinocytes, slowing growth

whyNot.A: That is **methotrexate**, given by mouth or injection for severe disease; his drug is a **cream applied to the plaques**
whyNot.B: That is **secukinumab**, an injected **antibody**; his drug is a **topical cream**
whyNot.C: That is how **tacrolimus and pimecrolimus** act; calcipotriene is a synthetic **calcitriol analogue**, not a calcineurin inhibitor
whyNot.D: That is **tazarotene**, a topical retinoid; calcipotriene is a **calcitriol analogue** that acts through a different nuclear receptor

answer: Binds the vitamin D receptor in keratinocytes (slows proliferation, promotes differentiation)
why: **Calcipotriene** is a **vitamin D3 analogue**: it binds the **vitamin D receptor** in keratinocytes, **slowing proliferation and restoring normal differentiation**, which thins the plaques. Excess use can raise calcium, so the amount applied is limited.

idea.rule: Topical psoriasis drugs normalize keratinocyte growth (vitamin D, retinoids) or suppress inflammation (steroids, calcineurin inhibitors).
also: Topical corticosteroids reduce inflammation and are first-line
Tazarotene is a topical retinoid for psoriasis
Coal tar and anthralin are older topical agents that slow keratinocyte proliferation
Methotrexate and biologics (TNF-alpha, IL-17, IL-23 inhibitors) are systemic options

drug.name: Calcipotriene (calcipotriol)
drug.how: Binds the vitamin D receptor in keratinocytes, slowing proliferation and promoting differentiation
drug.use: Plaque psoriasis (often combined with a topical corticosteroid)
drug.watch: Local irritation; hypercalcemia and hypercalciuria if used in large amounts
